title: Personal Liability, Protection and Induction Plan
summary: Brings the programme together by examining personal liability, the protections available to directors and a practical plan for the director's first year on the board.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Brings the programme together by examining personal liability, the protections available to directors and a practical plan for the director's first year on the board.
Learning Objectives: Identify the routes to personal regulatory, civil and criminal liability
Evaluate protections including indemnities, insurance and independent advice
Produce a personal induction and development plan
Syllabus: Enforcement against individuals: case studies and lessons
Indemnities, directors' and officers' insurance and independent advice
Record-keeping, dissent and when to resign
Workshop: the director's first-year induction plan
Intended Audience: Newly appointed non-executive, independent and executive directors of regulated firms
Directors moving into financial services from other sectors, or into a new type of regulated firm
Senior managers preparing for board appointment or approval by the authority
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Senior management or board experience is helpful. No prior experience of financial services regulation is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
FSB, Principles for an Effective Risk Appetite Framework (2013)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
